request.title: The Muscle Behind Puppy-Dog Eyes
request.provider_topic: Why do dogs have that expressive inner-eyebrow look?
request.narration: Puppy-dog eyes are anatomy, not just charm. That inner-brow lift comes from a small muscle: the levator anguli oculi medialis, above the inner corner of the eye. In 2019, researchers dissected four wolves and six dogs. The muscle was consistently present in the dogs they examined, and not in the wolves. Dogs also produced the eyebrow movement more often and more intensely than wolves. The highest intensities appeared only in dogs. The team suggests this may have given dogs an edge: a face that pulls at human sympathy. It is a hypothesis, not a proven cause. What is clear is that the muscle is part of dog anatomy, not a human invention. And the look works on us. Evolution shaped the plea; we answered it.
